frontmatter.title: Degree-two DQI on graph cycle codes
frontmatter.description: An explicit weight-two preparation and clean decoder, checked on a five-cycle, with a generation-only figure-eight and complete source-level accounting.

children.value: Decoded quantum interferometry (DQI) prepares a small collection of clause-error words, encodes their syndromes, and coherently erases the error register. A final Fourier transform combines the signed contributions into an objective-shaped assignment distribution
. Including pairs of clauses gives a quadratic filter: it changes the prepared state, the counter that controls preparation, and the decoder that must erase each pair.

This page implements those degree-two ingredients for binary graph cycle codes. The small example is a frustrated five-cycle, with every edge asking its endpoints to differ. Its optimum is available by a linear classical scan. The example makes coherent preparation, decoding and interference inspectable; it establishes no optimization advantage.
Accepted finite component and separate saved companion

On 14 November 2026, 170 focused pure tests passed, the five-cycle source circuit was generated, and its independent verifier completed one twelve-wire forward evolution, 512 Boolean clean-target decoder mappings and one small phase-exact CCX reference. A figure-eight circuit was exported separately without simulation. The original combined sequence then
, because serialized source arrays reached a client expecting text.

A separately reviewed saved-only continuation completed four ordinary Python notebook cells with execution counts 1–4. It joined source arrays in memory, preserved the original cell IDs/types and source projection, and displayed existing evidence. It repeated no tests, circuit generation, state evolution, decoder check or phase reference. The original failed sequence remains failed and spent. Acceptance covers the finite C5 component and this separate genuine companion; it is not a reclassification of the original whole sequence.

children.value: best-score/tie comparisons, and write the selected assignment plus the fixed root bit. C5’s cut

reaches four crossings; an odd cycle cannot cross all five edges. A linear scan constructs and verifies that optimum, while the all-zero cut scores zero. Alternating along both figure-eight cycles also gives its optimum in linear time. These baselines and the explicit access/preparation/readout costs are part of the task comparison.

C5’s kernel is the length-five repetition code after a syndrome-basis change, and its signs are affine-equivalent to an eligible repetition scaffold. The new mechanism is its degree-two state preparation and clean two-error circuit; it does not create a new hard code family.

children.value: regime quoted by Rosmanis version 1. That paper’s near-linear OPI result retains its QRAMC/QRAMQ access assumptions; this compiled ordinary graph circuit implements no such OPI memory model
The every-neighbor recovery premise in Apte and colleagues’ version 2 fails for

. Add a missing edge to make a weight-three word: its weight-two complement has the same syndrome, since the full five-cycle is a kernel word. This decoder returns the complement rather than that weight-three neighbor. Correct decoding of the prepared shell therefore does not meet that premise, and no semicircle theorem is used here. The paper’s field/channel/ensemble and classical-decoder qualifications remain attached to its results
. These two works are cited as exact preprint versions; peer-reviewed successors remain unverified in the project’s reading scope.

The generator, decoder, verifier and exposition are original project work. The scientific path uses Python’s standard library rather than an imported quantum SDK; its companion was executed with Python 3.12.14, ipykernel 7.4.0, nbclient 0.11.0 and nbformat 5.11.1. These ordinary notebook libraries are separate from quantum simulation, synthesis and resource-estimator calls. The Nature paper supplies DQI’s method, and its versioned supporting archive remains an external MIT reference whose author code/figures and benchmark were not adopted locally

Available verification is the retained finite numerical component, independent source/accounting reviews, saved-file bindings and separately executed ordinary companion. No local Lean, Rocq or other formal theorem has been reproduced. General input quality, fault-tolerant synthesis and physical resources remain planned, while the
retains its separate ideal and conditional physical evidence.
